What each approach does, in plain words

Press Explain to read how an approach works: once in plain words, once technically. Each team member writes their own in EXPLAIN.md in their experiment folder.

Page F2: did it point to the right pages of the rulebooks? 1.0 = every right page and nothing else. Missing a right page hurts more than adding a wrong one.

Clause F2: the same, but for the exact numbered rule (paragraph), not just the page. Stricter.

Regulation F2: did it pick the right rulebooks (here R48, R148, R150 and R10)?

Overfit risk: we have only one practice product with answers. "High" means the approach was tuned on that practice product and may score worse on the real, unseen one.

Standings

Only one labelled case exists, so a high score can mean fitted to it. Overfit risk comes from each experiment's risk.json plus automatic flags (exact gold match: high; no declaration: unknown). Prefer the lower-risk approach when scores are close. Clause F2 is stricter than page F2: it compares cited paragraphs with the gold paragraphs (official normalisation), so a neighbouring paragraph on the right page does not count and page-only citations score 0; "—" means the experiment's predictions.json is not the file that run scored. Click a header to sort.

Generalisation check: unseen product (holdout-acpe)

A different product the approaches were not built on: an Acceleration Control for Pedal Error system (driver-assistance software), answer key = 94 expert requirements from UN R175. Recall is the number to read: did it find the right rules on a product it never saw? Precision is understated here, because the key covers R175 only while a real ACPE product may also need EMC, cyber security or software-update rules. An approach that is strong on the rear lamp but weak here is probably overfitted.

Join and contribute

Any coding agent works: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, Codex / Cursor / most others read AGENTS.md, Gemini reads GEMINI.md, Copilot reads .github/copilot-instructions.md. Rules: pull before you push, work in your own experiment folder, declare overfit risk.

git clone https://github.com/LeonardoZambranoL/regulation-tl.git
git clone https://github.com/Certivity/industrial-ai-hackathon.git
cd regulation-tl
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
python -m pip install -r approaches/benchmarking/requirements.txt
git pull --rebase
python approaches/benchmarking/bench.py NAME approaches/experiments/NAME/outputs/predictions.json ../industrial-ai-hackathon/cases/dev-rear-lamp/expected.json --index ../industrial-ai-hackathon/regulations/index.json
python approaches/benchmarking/dashboard_rows.py
git pull --rebase
git add approaches && git commit -m "NAME: what changed"
git push

To see new results, run python approaches/dashboard/open.py from the repo root (pulls, then reopens this page).
